newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria far right rejects wooing from Euro-right.
newsitem.headline: Austria far right rejects wooing from Euro-right.

text.p: Austria's far right on Thursday rejected offers to link up with Flemish and French rightists in the European Parliament to establish an anti-Maastricht faction in the Strasbourg-based assembly.

Former Austria Alpine skiing team trainer Franz Linser, who topped the list of the nationalist Freedom Party in Austria's European elections on October 13, described calls to set up the faction by the Flemish rightwing Vlaams Blok party as "wishful thinking".

"There is not and has never been any desire on the part of the Freedom Party to open negotiations with extreme right groups and we reject their attempts to forge closer links with us," Linser said in a statement.
Linser said leading Vlaams Blok politician Filip Dewinter had called on the Freedom Party to sit with them and France's extreme right National Front in the European parliament.
"There is nothing that links us to these groups or their ideological views," Linser added.

The Freedom Party led by Joerg Haider won nearly 28 percent of the vote in the European election, its best result in a nationwide poll since Haider took over the leadership of the far right group 10 years ago.
The result gave them six seats in the EP, the same as the dominant Social Democrats of Chancellor Franz Vranitzky and just one behind the conservative People's Party.
During the election campaign, Haider called for a review of the Maastricht treaty and renegotiation of Austria's net $15 billion contribution to the European Union.
Haider, who laced his Euro-sceptic comments with anti-foreigner rhetoric, tapped a well of discontent in Austria over 22 months of EU membership.

The far right won huge backing from blue-collar voters, who have seen unemployment rise and foreign takeovers of Austrian firms since the Alpine republic joined the Brussels club in January last year.
